newsitem.title: UK: London freight rates end week shaky, volume light.
newsitem.headline: London freight rates end week shaky, volume light.

text.p: The dry cargo freight market ended the week very quietly with the BFI teetering on the edge of falling below the 1,000 level for the first time since August 4, 1987.
The volume of fixtures concluded was light. Some brokers were surprised that the index lost no more than two points on Friday to 1,001 since market conditions remain strongly in favour of charterers.
Shipping circles are full of discussions about the number and types of tonnage forced into lay-up although specific names of vessels involved are not readily available.

But there is little doubt that a fair number of larger, older units are "resting" in the vicinity or Piraeus. Even lay-up has its problems for owners, not least the estimated approximate daily cost of $1,500 daily covering skeleton crew, insurance, etc.

The main item of interest was reports from the Far East that Dreyfus fixed South Korean tonnage for 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for Oct 18/25 at $19.50/19.00 combo/no combo for Oct 18/25. This compares with $18.30 fixed by Halla last week for early Oct loading and was said by brokers to be a keen rate for loading a month hence.

Apart from a few handy-size orders there was little fresh grain business. Continental were believed to be indicating $16.50 for their enquiry last night for 50,000 heavy grains US Gulf/Aqaba for Sept 27/Oct 10 against tonnage at $17.50. Bunge quote only $8.00 for their Oct 5/10 three million cu ft heavy grain business US Gulf/Continent.

Pioneer have been linked with Ascona 64,000 dwt delivery Rotterdam end Sept for 2-4 months redelivery Atlantic at $6,500 daily, and Pan Ocean are reported to have fixed CSK Unity or Glory 65,000 dwt delivery US Gulf Oct 1/10 for 4-6 months at $7,700 daily (ballast bonus, if any, not known).

It emerged that Tradigrain recently fixed 25,000/5 wheat US Gulf/3 ports Peru at close to $13.00 basis 1-1. French charterers booked a prompt 20-year-old 33,000 dwt vessel for wheatflour from north France to the Red Sea at about $9,000 daily.

The minerals trades featured a number of fixtures which failed on subjects: Leopardi 120,000 coal Richards Bay/Rotterdam Nov 1/15 at $5.50 (Cobelfret), for example, and Hassbat Qatar 120,000 ironore Ubu/Rotterdam Oct 15/30 at $5.25 (Mosk).

Details were not available of alleged fixtures of Brazil Star 201,227 dwt to Keoyang delivery Atlantic for a Far East round and Iron Master for 1,000 tonnes ironore Narvik/Antwerp to Cobelfret. Cape Kestrel 160,000 dwt, open in the Far East, was said not to have fixed CRA's 150,000 ironore Dampier/Continent but other undisclosed business.

Hoogovens were believed to have concluded Transatlantic coal contracts over 3-5 years with Cargill and U Ming tonnage, but full information was lacking. Rumours that Leon 140,000 dwt was fixed by Cobelfret from Antwerp Oct 1/10 for a trip via Brazil to Revadanda at $8,000 daily were discounted by ME brokers.

Rumours circulated of activity from the Continent involving 40,000 dwt craned tonnage fixed for trips to the Far East at about $11,000 daily and to Brazil at close to $4,750 daily. There was also activity in the steels and fertilizer trades but details were kept private. Brokers reported weak chartering demand elsewhere for handies.

M and R were said to have booked Seastar II 28,234 dwt from South Africa to US Gulf or Atlantic at about $4,500 daily. Showa Fixeaspidoforos 35,055 dwt from Nopac early Oct to the Far East at close to $6,500 daily plus $100,000 bonus.
